memos.headline: MSFT and JPM Lead on Relative Strength; UNH in Freefall, GOOGL Breaking Down
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe as of May 9. MSFT is the standout leader—up 15% over four weeks, trading 12.4% above its 50-day and 6% above its 200-day mean, with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +13.7%, though RSI at 71.9 warns of near-term overbought risk. JPM is the second strongest name, sitting just 9.6% off its 52w high with positive 26-week returns of +12.8% and above both moving averages, suggesting institutional accumulation. On the other side, UNH is in outright collapse—RSI 23.6, down 36% in four weeks, 21.4% below its 50-day mean, and showing -43.5% relative strength vs SPY over four weeks; I would not try to catch this knife until price stabilizes above 420. GOOGL is also deteriorating with a -6.9% weekly drop, 26% off its high, and worsening relative strength, and I'd need to see it reclaim 160 to reconsider.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+13.7% vs SPY 12w), above both key averages, though RSI 71.9 suggests waiting for a pullback toward 420 before adding.
Above both 50d and 200d means, only 9.6% off 52w high with +12.8% 26w return; would reassess below 240.
RSI 23.6 and -36% in four weeks is a broken chart in freefall; no reason to step in until price holds above 420 for multiple sessions.
Down 6.9% this week, 26% off highs, below both averages with deteriorating relative strength of -7.6% vs SPY over 4 weeks; need a reclaim of 160 to reconsider.
Trading 12.3% below 200d mean with -9.7% 12w relative strength vs SPY; trend is clearly down and I'd need a close above 210 to turn neutral.
Recovering off lows with +8.4% 4w return but still 6.7% below 200d mean and 22% off highs; watching 120 as a level that could shift me to long.
Strong 4w bounce of +12.6% with positive relative strength vs SPY, but still 8.8% below 200d mean and 22% off highs—needs to clear 340 for conviction.
Flat 12w return and RSI 50.6 suggest a range-bound name; best relative strength vs SPY on a 12w basis (+6.4%) but no clear breakout setup.
RSI 38.2 with -11.2% 4w relative strength vs SPY; defensive name acting poorly, below both averages—would need a close above 163 to reconsider.
Middling setup—slightly above 50d mean but 3.1% below 200d, with -9.2% 12w relative strength; needs to reclaim 200 to turn constructive.

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Lead on Earnings Power; CAT and XOM Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in GOOGL and MSFT this quarter. GOOGL posted 38.3% net margins on 12% revenue growth with net income up 46% YoY, all on a modest $14.79B debt load — that is exceptional operating leverage. MSFT delivered 36.9% net margins, 13.3% revenue growth, and 17.7% net income growth with only $42.88B in debt, confirming the durability of its cloud-driven mix shift. On the other end, CAT's revenue fell 9.8% YoY with net income collapsing 29.8%, signaling serious cyclical headwinds and margin compression from $14.25B in revenue against $31.74B in total debt. XOM's flat revenue and -6.2% net income decline on a thin 9.3% margin leave little room for error if commodity prices soften further. I would need to see CAT's operating cash flow stabilize and XOM's margins recover before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 38.3% net margin, 46% YoY net income growth, and low leverage at $14.79B debt make this the best earnings-quality story in the universe.
36.9% net margin and 13.3% revenue growth with 17.7% net income growth demonstrate durable, high-quality earnings from the cloud mix shift.
Net income surged 64.2% YoY to $17.13B with margins expanding to 11.0%, but I want to see margin durability beyond one quarter before raising conviction.
56.2% net margin and 78% revenue growth are extraordinary, though the 10-K data is from January and I need the upcoming quarter to confirm the trajectory holds.
Revenue growth of only 5.1% and net income growth of 4.8% against $92.20B in total debt suggest limited upside from current fundamentals.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% net income growth, but bank-specific leverage ($407B debt) and macro sensitivity keep me at neutral.
Revenue declined 2.1% YoY with net income barely positive at +0.4%; defensive but not offering earnings growth at this point.
Revenue grew 9.8% to $109.58B but net margin is only 5.7% with $81.27B in debt and no comparable YoY net income figure disclosed — too opaque to take a directional view.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% YoY represent clear cyclical margin compression; I need stabilization in operating cash flow before reconsidering.
Flat revenue, -6.2% net income decline, and a thin 9.3% net margin leave no cushion if commodity prices weaken further.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Benign Inflation — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the macro regime as a prolonged pause with an easing bias: the Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three months while the unemployment rate has drifted up 20bp over the same period to 4.2%, and headline CPI is running at just 2.4% y/y. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+83bp over 12 months to +0.47pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual cuts, while the 10y yield at 4.37% has actually edged lower over three months. This combination — cooling labor market, contained inflation, a steepening curve — is constructive for duration-sensitive growth equities and modestly positive for banks via NIM expansion, but I am cautious on late-cycle industrials and energy given the demand-side softening signal from rising unemployment. A surprise uptick in the next CPI print above 3% y/y or a payroll surge that pushes unemployment back below 4.0% would flip my regime call back to 'hawkish hold' and hurt long-duration positioning.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits from easing bias and falling long-end yields; benign CPI supports multiples.
Similar duration tailwind as MSFT; slightly lower conviction given consumer exposure to a softening labor market.
High-duration growth name that should re-rate positively as the curve prices in cuts, though elevated vol warrants some caution.
Benefits from lower discount rates, but consumer-facing revenue could feel drag from rising unemployment at 4.2%.
Ad-driven revenue is cyclically sensitive, but the easing-bias macro backdrop and contained inflation support the multiple.
Steepening curve (+83bp y/y in 10y-2y spread) supports NIM, but rising unemployment and potential credit deterioration cap upside.
Defensive staple is a wash: benign CPI preserves margins, but the easing-bias regime favors growth over defensives.
Defensive healthcare name with limited macro sensitivity; no strong directional call from current data.
Late-cycle industrial faces headwinds from softening labor market and potential demand slowdown signaled by rising unemployment.
Energy is vulnerable to demand-side weakness implied by rising unemployment; no inflation tailwind with CPI at only 2.4% y/y.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: MSFT and JPM Positive Momentum vs. UNH and AAPL Negative Tone Shifts
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal available this cycle. MSFT's +7.6% reaction to its 4/30 results is the strongest positive tone shift in the group, suggesting narrative momentum that may not yet be fully priced given the magnitude. JPM's +4.0% earnings-day pop in mid-April set a constructive tone for financials early in the season. On the negative side, UNH's catastrophic -22.4% post-earnings drop on 4/17 followed by a C-suite departure filing on 4/29 signals a deeply damaged narrative where sentiment may still be deteriorating. AAPL's -3.7% reaction to its 5/1 results and PG's identical -3.7% earnings drop suggest consumer-facing names are under pressure, though these are more modest declines that could already be absorbed.

views.note: The +7.6% post-earnings reaction is the strongest positive sentiment signal in the universe, indicating a narrative upgrade that likely has room to run.
A -22.4% earnings-day collapse followed by executive departure filing signals a severely negative sentiment regime that is unlikely to reverse quickly.
The +4.0% earnings reaction was constructive but occurred nearly a month ago, so the positive tone shift may already be priced in.
The -3.7% post-earnings reaction suggests negative sentiment tone, though the decline is moderate enough that it could stabilize.
A +1.7% earnings reaction plus a flurry of subsequent 8-K filings suggest active corporate narrative management and mildly positive tone.
The -3.7% earnings drop mirrors AAPL's negative tone, and the defensive staples narrative appears under pressure this cycle.
A muted +0.6% earnings reaction and two executive change filings give no clear directional sentiment signal.
A flat +0.4% earnings reaction suggests sentiment is balanced with no clear narrative shift to trade.
Only a non-earnings 8-K filing is available with no price reaction data, leaving me without a clear sentiment read ahead of its upcoming report.
A near-flat -0.1% post-earnings reaction suggests the market had already priced in the narrative, leaving no actionable sentiment edge.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Export-Control Risk Persist Despite VIX Retreat; Favor Domestically-Oriented Names
memos.body: I note that while the VIX has collapsed 57% over the past month to 22.48, the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index remains stubbornly high at 567.82, essentially flat month-over-month and still reflecting a structurally elevated policy-risk environment. High-yield OAS at 3.51% has tightened 106 bps in a month but is still 84 bps wider on a 3-month basis, suggesting credit markets are pricing residual geopolitical tail risk. WTI crude at $61.25 is down 14% over three months, which I read as demand-side concern tied to China-related trade friction rather than supply relief—this weighs on energy earnings but benefits consumer-facing names. NVDA's mid-April 8-K (8.01 Other Events) likely relates to export-control disclosures affecting advanced AI chip shipments to China, a structural headwind I cannot dismiss until we see a concrete policy reversal. I have higher conviction in domestically-anchored franchises like PG and JPM and remain cautious on names with heavy China/semiconductor supply-chain exposure.

views.note: Export-control overhang on AI chips to China is structural; April 8-K signals ongoing regulatory disclosure and I need a clear policy rollback to turn constructive.
Heavy China manufacturing concentration is a known risk under elevated policy uncertainty, but no fresh 8-K filings give me directional conviction either way.
Domestically-oriented consumer staple with pricing power; three 8-K filings in recent weeks suggest active investor communication, and lower crude helps input costs.
Steeper 10y-2y curve (+27 bps over 3 months) supports NIM, and as a domestic financial franchise it is less exposed to trade-policy shocks than tech.
WTI at $61.25 is down 14% in three months, pressuring upstream margins; energy security tailwinds exist but demand uncertainty from China trade friction caps upside.
Global capex cycle is vulnerable to trade-policy disruption; elevated policy uncertainty index at 568 and softening crude signal weaker industrial demand ahead.

RSI at 71.9 is the only caution, so stop is set at ~1 ATR.

Domestic franchise limits geopolitical exposure.
